summary: The cardholder starts with no balance, makes purchases that push the account above the numeric credit limit, and then reaches statement close while still over limit. The scenario is designed to probe over-limit status at statement close while also including obligation-linked events for credit-limit, grace-period, and minimum-payment clauses, with the payment obligation intentionally left unmet after the statement.
assumptions: The account opens this cycle with a $500 numeric credit limit and a $0 previous balance.
All purchase transactions are authorized and posted during the same billing cycle before the statement closes.

The issuer allows purchases that cumulatively exceed the credit limit so the account can be over limit at statement close, even though clause.4.credit_limits says the cardholder promises not to cause this result.
No payments are made before the statement closes, so the statement new balance remains above the credit limit.
The prior cycle was paid in full or there was no previous balance, so the issuer's 25-day purchase grace period applies for this cycle.

A payment due date exists after the statement close, but this archetype ends before any actual payment is made; the minimum-payment obligation is therefore included as an unmet obligation event/notice rather than a performing payment.

Although the contract text also contains inconsistent disclosure language about over-the-credit-limit fees, this scenario focuses only on over-limit status at statement close and does not model any fee assessment.
